skill: Nonlinear Equations In One Variable And Systems Of Equations In Two Variables
prompt:
$$y = 6 p ( q + 11 )$$

The given equation relates the positive numbers $p$, $q$, and $y$. Which equation correctly expresses $p$ in terms of $q$ and $y$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. To express $p$ in terms of $q$ and $y$, the given equation can be rewritten so that $p$ is isolated on one side. Since $q$ is positive, $q + 11$ is not equal to zero. Dividing both sides of the given equation by $6\left(q + 11\right)$ yields $\frac{y}{6\left(q + 11\right)} = p$, or $p = \frac{y}{6\left(q + 11\right)}$.
